name: Short-term reversal in stocks (one-month losers beat winners)

origin.source_title: Evidence of Predictable Behavior of Security Returns (Journal of Finance 45(3), 881-898)

how_it_works.simple: Buy the stocks that fell most last month and sell the ones that rose most; over the next month they tend to swap back.
how_it_works.analogy: Like a crowded doorway: people pushed out of the way last month drift back in.
how_it_works.precise: Monthly returns of individual stocks are negatively related to the previous month's return (and positively to returns 12 months back). Sorting stocks into deciles on a forecast built from these patterns gives a large spread in next-month returns. The usual explanation is that liquidity providers are paid for absorbing order imbalances.

rule: At each month end, rank stocks by the past month's return; buy the bottom decile and sell the top decile for one month.
data_needed: Monthly stock returns (the Kenneth French data library has a free short-term reversal factor)
economic_rationale: Prices overshoot when traders demand liquidity, and the investors who absorb that demand are paid when prices bounce back.
why_it_might_fail: Turnover is close to 100% a month, so trading costs eat much of the profit, especially in small stocks. Part of the effect is bid-ask bounce rather than a tradable return.

reported_results.notes: The abstract reports that the difference in abnormal returns between the extreme deciles of stocks sorted on predicted returns was 2.49 percent per month. Before costs. Sorted on a regression forecast, not only last month's return.

post_publication_evidence: Not checked by us yet. Later work on whether the profits survive trading costs exists; we have not read it.

relevance.reason: A classic anomaly that many mean-reversion bots trade; a free factor series makes a quick comparison possible.

research.notes: The free series is a published factor, not our own sort, so a test would check the factor before costs. Added by Amanda's library batch on 2026-10-25 (options, intraday and equity anomalies that retail traders and bots claim to use).
